"'''Alone'''" is a song written by [[Billy Steinberg]] and [[Tom Kelly (musician)|Tom Kelly]], who recorded it under the name i‑Ten for their 1983 album ''[[Taking a Cold Look]]''. It was later recorded by actress Valerie Stevenson and actor [[John Stamos]] for the original soundtrack of the [[CBS]] [[Situation comedy|sitcom]] ''[[Dreams (TV series)|Dreams]]'' in 1984. American [[Rock music|rock]] band [[Heart (band)|Heart]] recorded the song for their 1987 album ''[[Bad Animals]]'', and their version reached number one in the United States and Canada. In 2007, [[Celine Dion]] recorded it for her album ''[[Taking Chances]]''. In 2010, [[Alyssa Reid]] used the music and lyrics for the chorus of her song "[[Alone Again (Alyssa Reid song)|Alone Again]]".

"Alone" is a song written by Billy Steinberg and Tom Kelly, who recorded it under the name i‑Ten for their 1983 album Taking a Cold Look. It was later recorded by actress Valerie Stevenson and actor John Stamos for the original soundtrack of the CBS sitcom Dreams in 1984. American rock band Heart recorded the song for their 1987 album Bad Animals, and their version reached number one in the United States and Canada. In 2007, Celine Dion recorded it for her album Taking Chances. In 2010, Alyssa Reid used the music and lyrics for the chorus of her song "Alone Again".

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: "Alone" is a [[rock ballad]] written by [[Billy Steinberg]] and [[Tom Kelly (musician)|Tom Kelly]], who recorded it under the name i‑Ten for their 1983 album ''[[Taking a Cold Look]]''. It appears as the third track on the album. The release attracted little attention, and i‑Ten did not record any further albums before disbanding.

sections.heading: ''Dreams'' version
sections.wikitext: In late 1984, actress Valerie Stevenson and actor [[John Stamos]] recorded the song for the [[CBS]] [[Situation comedy|sitcom]] ''[[Dreams (TV series)|Dreams]]'' in their roles as Lisa Copley and Gino Minnelli. It appears in the episode of the same name, in which the band perform the song for Frank and Louise's anniversary party. It is the earliest cover of the song. In the episode, Frank and Gino write a poem and develop it into a song. The episode aired on November 7, 1984. The song was released as a single on the same day, but it did not chart.

[[Heart (band)|Heart]] released the song as the lead single from their ninth studio album, ''[[Bad Animals]]'', on May 16, 1987. Their recording is a [[power ballad]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/music/what-to-listen-to/21-best-power-ballads/alone/ |title=Bonnie Tyler's Total Eclipse of the Heart and the 20 other best power ballads |date=July 23, 2015 |access-date=April 24, 2021 |website=Telegraph.co.uk}}</ref> that opens with a piano introduction and a restrained vocal by [[Ann Wilson]], building into a synth‑driven hard‑rock chorus. Tom Kelly, the song's co‑writer and an experienced session vocalist, provided the high harmony parts on the track.<ref name="songfacts">{{cite web |url=http://www.songfacts.com/detail.php?id=3737 |title=Alone |work=Songfacts.com |access-date=October 5, 2009}}</ref>

"Alone" reached number one on both the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and the US [[Cash Box Top 100|''Cash Box'' Top 100]]. It peaked at number three on the [[UK Singles Chart]]. Internationally, it topped the chart in Canada, reached the top five in Ireland, Norway, and Switzerland, the top 10 in Australia, Belgium, and the Netherlands, and the top 20 in West Germany. An unplugged version later appeared on Heart's 1995 album ''The Road Home''. An extended 5:30 version was issued on the Japanese 3‑inch CD of the album's third single, "[[There's the Girl]]".<ref>{{cite AV media notes |title=There's the Girl |year=1988 |type=Japanese 3-inch CD single liner notes |publisher=Capitol |id=CP10-2001}}</ref>

''[[Cash Box]]'' described the track as "a potent, emotion‑drenched rock ballad that features Ann Wilson's signature billowing, riveting vocal performance".<ref name="cb">{{cite magazine |title=Single Releases |url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/80s/1987/CB-1987-05-09.pdf |magazine=Cash Box |date=May 9, 1987 |access-date=August 8, 2022 |page=9}}</ref> The song earned Heart a nomination for the [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Duo or Group]] at the [[30th Annual Grammy Awards]].

Heart released the song as the lead single from their ninth studio album, Bad Animals, on May 16, 1987. Their recording is a power ballad that opens with a piano introduction and a restrained vocal by Ann Wilson, building into a synth‑driven hard‑rock chorus. Tom Kelly, the song's co‑writer and an experienced session vocalist, provided the high harmony parts on the track.

"Alone" reached number one on both the US Billboard Hot 100 and the US Cash Box Top 100. It peaked at number three on the UK Singles Chart. Internationally, it topped the chart in Canada, reached the top five in Ireland, Norway, and Switzerland, the top 10 in Australia, Belgium, and the Netherlands, and the top 20 in West Germany. An unplugged version later appeared on Heart's 1995 album The Road Home. An extended 5:30 version was issued on the Japanese 3‑inch CD of the album's third single, "There's the Girl".

Cash Box described the track as "a potent, emotion‑drenched rock ballad that features Ann Wilson's signature billowing, riveting vocal performance". The song earned Heart a nomination for the Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Duo or Group at the 30th Annual Grammy Awards.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video, directed by [[Marty Callner]], was released in June 1987. It begins with Ann standing on a balcony singing to Nancy below on stage playing the piano, echoing the ''[[Romeo and Juliet]]'' balcony scene. Ann then appears dressed entirely in black, including a veil and gown. The sisters are shown performing the chorus on stage, where Nancy's piano collapses at the first impact of the chorus. During the second verse, Nancy plays a piano placed within a deteriorated set. She is later shown riding a black horse. Ann appears again in the all‑black outfit within the broken set, before the video cuts back to the stage performance for the song's climax. As the track fades, Ann and Nancy face each other, followed by a final close‑up of Ann before the screen goes dark.

Celine Dion recorded "Alone" for her tenth English‑language studio album, Taking Chances (2007). Issued as the second single in Europe and North America, and as the third in the United Kingdom in 2008, the track was produced by Ben Moody, former member of Evanescence. Dion's version received generally positive reviews and charted in several countries, including Canada, the United Kingdom, and Sweden.

sections.heading: Background and release
sections.wikitext: Dion recorded "Alone" in 2007 for ''[[Taking Chances]]'', with production by [[Ben Moody]], previously of [[Evanescence]].<ref name="idolator">{{cite news |title=Celine Dion / Ben Moody Collaboration |url=http://idolator.com/310835/310835 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125215922/http://idolator.com/310835/310835 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 25, 2013 |access-date=October 17, 2012 |newspaper=[[Idolator (website)|Idolator]]}}</ref> Her recording incorporates piano and string arrangements.<ref name="idolator" /> It was released as the second single in Europe and North America, and as the third in the United Kingdom. The UK digital release on May 5, 2008, coincided with the British leg of the [[Taking Chances World Tour]].<ref name="itunes">{{cite web |title=iTunes - Music - Alone - Single by Céline Dion |url=https://itunes.apple.com/gb/album/alone-single/id277913218 |publisher=[[iTunes Store]] |access-date=October 17, 2012}}</ref> In October 2008, "Alone" was included on the European edition of ''[[My Love: Essential Collection]]''.<ref name="essential">{{cite web |title=The Essential |publisher=Exlibris.ch |url=http://www.exlibris.ch/musik/cd/celine-dion/the-essential/?id=0886979367722 |language=de |access-date=July 15, 2011}}</ref> A live version appears on ''[[Taking Chances World Tour: The Concert]]''.<ref name="allmusictaking">{{cite web |last=Erlewine |first=Stephen Thomas |title=Taking Chances World Tour: The Concert : AllMusic |url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/taking-chances-world-tour-the-concert-mw0001972873 |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=August 12, 2012}}</ref>
sections.text: Dion recorded "Alone" in 2007 for Taking Chances, with production by Ben Moody, previously of Evanescence. Her recording incorporates piano and string arrangements. It was released as the second single in Europe and North America, and as the third in the United Kingdom. The UK digital release on May 5, 2008, coincided with the British leg of the Taking Chances World Tour. In October 2008, "Alone" was included on the European edition of My Love: Essential Collection. A live version appears on Taking Chances World Tour: The Concert.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: "Alone" received generally positive reviews, with several critics praising Dion's vocal performance and the song's melodic appeal. [[Stephen Thomas Erlewine]] of [[AllMusic]] named it one of the album's standout tracks, praising Dion's energetic interpretation of [[Heart (band)|Heart]]'s original and noting the song's pronounced stylistic shifts.<ref name="allmusicreview">Erlewine, Stephen (November 17, 2007) [http://www.allmusic.com/album/taking-chances-r1213654/review Taking Chances - Review {{pipe}} Allmusic] [[AllMusic]] – ''[[Rovi|Rovi Corporation]]'' Retrieved February 28, 2011.</ref> Sarah Rodman of ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' described the performance as a "great vocal, terrific melody, a fine rendition", while observing that the song remains closely associated with Heart's [[Ann Wilson]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rodman |first=Sarah |date=November 13, 2007 |title=Dion takes few risks on 'Chances' |url=http://archive.boston.com/ae/music/cd_reviews/articles/2007/11/13/dion_takes_few_risks_on_chances/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730130456/http://www.boston.com/ae/music/cd_reviews/articles/2007/11/13/dion_takes_few_risks_on_chances/ |archive-date=July 30, 2012 |access-date=July 18, 2025 |website=[[Boston Globe]] |url-access=registration}}</ref> ''[[Toronto Star]]'' editor Ashante Infantry called the track "sentimental", and [[Chuck Taylor (writer and editor)|Chuck Taylor]] of ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' described it as "a rowdy cover".<ref name="Billboard">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/content_display/reviews/albums/e3idd293825dd51c45c4645602dffc3375a |title=Taking Chances - Billboard Review |last=Taylor |first=Chuck |magazine=Billboard |access-date=March 10, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071111120205/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/content_display/reviews/albums/e3idd293825dd51c45c4645602dffc3375a |archive-date=November 11, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
sections.text: "Alone" received generally positive reviews, with several critics praising Dion's vocal performance and the song's melodic appeal. Stephen Thomas Erlewine of AllMusic named it one of the album's standout tracks, praising Dion's energetic interpretation of Heart's original and noting the song's pronounced stylistic shifts. Sarah Rodman of The Boston Globe described the performance as a "great vocal, terrific melody, a fine rendition", while observing that the song remains closely associated with Heart's Ann Wilson. Toronto Star editor Ashante Infantry called the track "sentimental", and Chuck Taylor of Billboard described it as "a rowdy cover".

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: "Alone" debuted at number 85 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and remained for two weeks.<ref name="ukchart" /> It sold 12,535 copies in the United States, entering the [[Bubbling Under Hot 100 Singles]] at number 24 and the [[Canadian Hot 100]] at number 57. It also entered the [[Sverigetopplistan|Swedish Singles Chart]] due to digital sales, peaking at number 52.<ref name="sweden">{{cite web |author=Steffen Hung |url=http://swedishcharts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=C%E9line+Dion&titel=Alone&cat=s |title=Swedish Singles Chart |publisher=Swedishcharts.com |access-date=May 12, 2012}}</ref>

Retrieved March 7, 2008.</ref> Dion promoted the song in France on ''[[Star Academy]]''. On November 23, 2007, she appeared on ''[[The View (U.S. TV series)|The View]]'' to perform "[[Taking Chances (song)|Taking Chances]]" and "Alone".<ref name="celinenews4">{{cite news |title=Celine Performing on The View! |url=http://www.celinedion.com/ca/node/70132 |access-date=September 15, 2012 |newspaper=Celine Dion Web |date=November 22, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228183532/http://www.celinedion.com/ca/node/70132 |archive-date=December 28, 2014}}</ref> She performed the song during most dates of the ''[[Taking Chances World Tour]]'', and the performance appears on ''[[Taking Chances World Tour: The Concert]]''.<ref name="allmusictaking" />

She performed the song during most dates of the Taking Chances World Tour, and the performance appears on Taking Chances World Tour: The Concert.
